title: What happens if an entire class of workers loses faith in their careers
titleZh: 如果整个阶层的工人对自己的职业失去信心会发生什么
author: RickJWagner
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Credits Aaron Horwath is the director of AI operations at a creative technology company where he is focused on implementing AI in a way that supports both humans and business.

On a recent morning commute, I sat on a train in one of those awkward four-person configurations with a shared table. Across from me sat a typical commuter: early 30s, slacks, dress shirt, dirty white sneakers, hair a little disheveled, AirPods in, basking in the glow of an open MacBook.

For over half an hour, I listened to this young man as he was on a call explaining, in painfully monotone detail, EBITDAs, margin expansion opportunities, cost structures, ARR, etc. On and on he went until the screeching of the train’s brakes signaled our arrival at the final station. But as everyone else around us began shuffling to disembark, I watched the man begin digging frantically through a leather bag at his side. Intriguing! I wondered what he’d pull out. A copy of “Atomic Habits”? A framed portrait of Gary V? A Mac mini running OpenClaw?

None of the above. Instead, he took out two long knitting needles. Between them dangled a mound of pink yarn. He explained to me that he was making a winter hat for a niece. And for the first time that morning, I noticed a glint of pride and excitement in his eyes.
The hat was a project born from a desire, as he put it, to do something.
summaryZh: Credits Aaron Horwath is the director of AI operations at a creative technology company where he is focused on implementing AI in a way that supports both humans and business.

comments.author: Animats
comments.textRawHtml:
Addressing the question in the title, "What happens if an entire class of workers loses faith in their careers", look at what happened to printers. That was a good skilled trade for centuries. Then it just went away. Phototypesetting took the high volume end. Desktop publishing took the low end. Computer-controlled presses took press operators. And then the newspaper business died.

I've heard homeless former printers talking about the good days at the Burger King near the cable car turntable at Powell and Market. They thought they had careers. Now they're struggling to survive.

Knitting is not the answer. This is a survival issue. Somehow I suspect the author inherited money.
comments.textZhHtml:
解决标题中的问题“如果整个阶级的工人对自己的职业失去信心会发生什么”，看看打印机发生了什么。几个世纪以来，这一直是一项良好的熟练贸易。然后它就消失了。照相排版占据了高产量。桌面出版占据了低端市场。计算机控制的印刷机取代了印刷机操作员。然后报纸生意就消亡了。

我听到无家可归的前印刷商谈论在鲍威尔和市场缆车转盘附近的汉堡王的美好时光。他们以为自己有事业。 现在他们正在为生存而挣扎。

编织不是答案。这是一个生存问题。不知怎的，我怀疑作者继承了钱。

children.author: estearum
children.textRawHtml:
Surprised no one has made the extremely obvious observation that it took literal centuries for printing technology to eliminate the trade of printers, which could not have possibly have employed more than 0.01% of people at its peak.

Compared to the potential obsolescence of 40% to 60% of the US workforce over the course of 10 - 20 years?

You can argue about whether the obsolescence is real or not, but if it is, the plight of the printers is totally incomparable.

Question: What happens when you drive a car at 90 mph into a concrete wall?

Answer: Well, actually just this morning pulling into my parking spot, I bumped into the barrier beneath my tires. It was fine!
children.textZhHtml:
令人惊讶的是，没有人做出极其明显的观察，即印刷技术花了几个世纪的时间才消除了打印机贸易，而打印机在其巅峰时期雇用的人口不可能超过 0.01%。

与 10 - 20 年间美国劳动力 40% 到 60% 的潜在淘汰相比？

你可以争论这种淘汰是真实的还是不是，但是如果是，打印机的困境是完全无法比拟的。

问题：当你以 90 英里/小时的速度驾驶汽车撞上混凝土墙时会发生什么？

答案：嗯，实际上就在今天早上，我把车开进停车位时，就撞到了轮胎下面的护栏上。很好！

children.author: thegrim33
children.textRawHtml: The difference is that one of those things actually happened, and the other one is your hypothetical extremist/exaggerated/worst possible case of what might happen this time.
children.textZhHtml: 区别在于，其中一件事确实发生了，另一件事是您假设的极端/夸张/最糟糕的情况，这一次可能会发生。

children.author: estearum
children.textRawHtml: the wise man bowed his head solemnly and spoke: "theres actually zero reason to think about events that haven't happened yet. you imbecile. you fucking moron"
children.textZhHtml: 智者郑重地低下了头，说道：“其实没有理由去思考尚未发生的事情。你这个白痴。你他妈的白痴”

children.author: altmanaltman
children.textRawHtml: Yeah + the world was much different than it is today. It trivializes the risk by saying we have seen it before and we were okay when its a fundamentally different problem in many aspects.
children.textZhHtml: 是的，当时的世界与今天有很大不同。它轻视了风险，说我们以前见过这种情况，而且我们没问题，但实际上它在很多方面都是一个根本不同的问题。

children.author: Macha
children.textRawHtml: Also fails to distinguish between “society came out of it fine” (generally true) and “individuals came out of it fine” (much more mixed of a track record)
children.textZhHtml: 也无法区分“社会一切顺利”（通常是正确的）和“个人一切顺利”（业绩记录更加复杂）

children.author: rayiner
children.textRawHtml: Yes. And individuals largely don’t come out fine. We have this notion of “retraining” but that’s not real. It’s like how studies show it’s very hard to make friends as an adult. Most people whose jobs were shipped overseas in deindustrialization never recovers.
children.textZhHtml: 是的。个人基本上都不会好起来。我们有“再培训”的概念，但这不是真实的。就像研究表明成年人很难交朋友一样。大多数在去工业化过程中工作被转移到海外的人永远无法恢复。

children.author: lesuorac
children.textRawHtml:
> We have this notion of “retraining” but that’s not real.

While I haven't been "retrained" my understanding was the real issue that it's lip-service.

Like the Department of Labor doesn't actually show up to a closed down factory with staff to train people in some other vocation.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我们有“再培训”的概念，但这不是真实的。

虽然我没有接受过“再培训”，但我的理解是真正的问题是它只是口头上的。

就像劳工部实际上并没有带着员工出现在一家关闭的工厂来培训其他职业的人员一样。

children.author: logicchains
children.textRawHtml: University-educated "Knowledge workers" should be much more capable of learning new things than the average factory production line worker.
children.textZhHtml: 受过大学教育的“知识工人”应该比普通工厂生产线工人更有能力学习新事物。

children.author: chongli
children.textRawHtml:
How is the GGP post (by Animats) trivializing the risk? They're saying "it's a survival issue" and saying the printers became homeless and struggling to feed themselves.

Sounds much more like a warning than a dismissal to me. If 40-50% of the workforce ends up like that then we're living in a post-apocalyptic wasteland failed state.
children.textZhHtml:
GGP 帖子（Animats 发布）是如何淡化风险的？他们说“这是一个生存问题”，并说印刷商无家可归，难以养活自己。

对我来说，这听起来更像是警告，而不是解雇。如果 40-50% 的劳动力最终变成这样，那么我们就生活在一个后世界末日的荒地失败状态。

children.author: rayiner
children.textRawHtml:
> If 40-50% of the workforce ends up like that then we're living in a post-apocalyptic wasteland failed state.

I a lot less than that. Most people don’t have jobs that can be done remotely, which I think is a good proxy for the ceiling of who can be replaced by AI. Almost nobody on my block besides me is going to be replaced (beer brewer, several nurses, navy servicemen, cops, and teachers).
children.textZhHtml:
> 如果 40-50% 的劳动力最终都是这样，那么我们就生活在一个后世界末日的荒地失败状态。

我比这要少得多。大多数人没有可以远程完成的工作，我认为这很好地体现了人工智能可以取代谁的上限。除了我之外，我所在街区几乎没有人会被取代（啤酒酿造商、几名护士、海军军人、警察和教师）。

children.author: Recurecur
children.textRawHtml:
I think you’re failing to factor in the rapid improvement in robotics.

I was at the hospital a few days ago, and was pondering the numerous nurses who were wheeling around portable nursing stations with monitors and various types of equipment. They’d stop at a room, take a patient’s blood pressure (among various other things), type some notes, and move on. I can easily imagine most nursing tasks being subsumed by robotics.

The same goes for brewers, soldiers, cops, and teachers. Soldier, cop, and teacher robots are already being tested, or actually deployed…and it’s early yet. If a safe, highly dense source of power is developed, that will vastly accelerate the process. At best, there will be far fewer humans involved, monitoring the robots, much as software engineers are now monitoring the agentic AIs.

I’m not sure how human society will adapt. The optimistic view (championed by Elon Musk) is that we’re headed for a “Star Trek economy” of essentially endless abundance for everyone. I hope things play out somewhere along those lines…

I’ve personally been impacted very heavily by LLM technology. Two of my major skills, coding and writing, have been greatly devalued by it. I’m relying on one of the truly core human traits to compensate - adaptability. That’s an area where LLMs currently lag far behind.

We’ll see how things go from here… ;-)
children.textZhHtml:
我认为你没有考虑到机器人技术的快速进步。

几天前我在医院，思考着众多带着监视器和各种类型的设备在便携式护理站周围转来转去的护士。他们会在一个房间停下来，测量病人的血压（以及其他一些事情），写下一些笔记，然后继续前进。我可以很容易地想象大多数护理任务都被机器人所取代。

酿酒师、士兵、警察和教师也是如此。士兵、警察和教师机器人已经在测试或实际部署……而且还为时过早。如果开发出一种安全、高密度的能源，那将大大加速这一进程。充其量，参与监控机器人的人员将会少得多，就像软件工程师现在监控代理人工智能一样。

我不确定人类社会将如何适应。乐观的观点（由埃隆·马斯克倡导）是，我们正在走向一种“星际迷航经济”，为每个人带来本质上无尽的富足。我希望事情能沿着这些方向发展……

我个人受到法学硕士技术的影响很大。我的两项主要技能，编码和写作，已经被它大大贬值了。我依靠人类真正核心的特质之一来弥补——适应性。这是法学硕士目前远远落后的领域。

我们将看看事情如何发展……;-)

children.author: kaffekaka
children.textRawHtml:
> I can easily imagine most nursing tasks being subsumed by robotics

I think you are greatly underestimating the difficulty of automating nursing tasks.

About teachers: some amount teaching profession can be automated, but the parts that cannot (in any reasonable way in the foreseeable future) are perhaps the most core aspects of teaching.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我可以很容易地想象大多数护理任务都被机器人技术所涵盖

我认为你大大低估了自动化护理任务的难度。

关于教师：一些教学职业可以自动化，但不能（在可预见的未来以任何合理的方式）的部分可能是教学的最核心方面。

children.author: Recurecur
children.textRawHtml:
We shall see about how much of nursing can be automated. I do think that the human presence of a nurse (particularly if of the opposite sex to the patient) is helpful. That could still be provided on a less frequent basis.

As to the rest of their function, I think probably the biggest obstacle will be the ability to safely manipulate the human body, as in turning or moving the patient. That requires delicacy, advanced tactile sensors, and physical power. For fine detail work, such as finding a vein with a needle, the technology already exists. Elon Musk also predicts that robotic surgery will rapidly outpace human surgeons, and I agree there.

On the subject of human teachers, my comment is similar to that about human nurses. A human connection helps with motivation. That said, I think video serves much the same function, and with video one teacher can reach an unlimited number of classrooms. That’s independent of how humanistic the teaching robots will become, and I expect that will also improve rapidly. We are nearing singularity like situations with engineering problems, in other words recursive improvement without much if any human intervention.
children.textZhHtml:
我们将了解有多少护理可以实现自动化。我确实认为护士在场（尤其是与患者异性的护士）是有帮助的。这仍然可以以较低的频率提供。

至于它们的其余功能，我认为最大的障碍可能是安全操纵人体的能力，例如转动或移动患者。这需要精致、先进的触觉传感器和体力。对于精细工作，例如用针寻找静脉，该技术已经存在。埃隆·马斯克还预测机器人手术将迅速超过人类外科医生，我对此表示同意。

关于人类教师的问题，我的评论与人类护士的评论类似。人际关系有助于激励。也就是说，我认为视频具有大致相同的功能，通过视频，一名教师可以覆盖无限数量的教室。这与教学机器人的人性化程度无关，我预计这也会迅速改善。我们正接近工程问题的奇点，换句话说，无需太多人为干预即可实现递归改进。

children.author: buddhistdude
children.textRawHtml: What does it matter how difficult it is? That only means it's gonna take a while longer.
children.textZhHtml: 难度有多大又有什么关系呢？这仅意味着需要更长的时间。

children.author: rayiner
children.textRawHtml:
That’s not how technology works. We went from first flight in 1903 to a man on the moon in 1969. Then we basically did almost nothing in aerospace for the next 50 years. We never got past the supersonic barrier for feasible commercial air travel. Apart from somewhat worse fuel efficiency, a 747 from 1969 can achieve basically the same trips in the same amount of time as a 787 or A350.

What looks like exponential curves turn into S-shaped curves everywhere. In the last century, coal power plants have gotten less than twice as efficient. A professor at law school was giving a lecture on technological singularity back in 2011. And I pointed out that Moore’s law was already dead. And in fact in the decade since then improvements came far slower than they did from 1990-2000.
children.textZhHtml:
技术不是这样运作的。从1903年首次飞行到1969年载人登月。接下来的50年里，我们在航空航天领域几乎没有做任何事情。我们从未突破过可行的商业航空旅行的超音速障碍。除了燃油效率稍差之外，1969 年生产的 747 可以在相同的时间内实现与 787 或 A350 基本相同的行程。

看起来指数曲线到处都变成了 S 形曲线。在上个世纪，燃煤电厂的效率还不到两倍。早在 2011 年，法学院的一位教授就技术奇点做了一次演讲。我指出摩尔定律已经失效了。事实上，此后的十年里，进步的速度比 1990 年至 2000 年要慢得多。

children.author: somenameforme
children.textRawHtml: When things are spread out over time people are able to adjust to the point that society, as a whole, might not even notice there was a problem, even if for some segment of that society it might feel like the end of the world - or at least an incomparable inflection point. The only real problem you have is when things come on hard and fast, like a tsunami.
children.textZhHtml: 当事情随着时间的推移而分散时，人们能够适应到整个社会甚至可能没有注意到存在问题的程度，即使对于社会的某些部分来说，这可能感觉像是世界末日 - 或者至少是一个无与伦比的拐点。你遇到的唯一真正的问题是当事情突然来临时，就像海啸一样。

children.author: soulofmischief
children.textRawHtml: Right now, many people do not own property and are one missed paycheck away from homelessness.
children.textZhHtml: 现在，许多人没有财产，只要少付一点薪水就可能无家可归。

children.author: rayiner
children.textRawHtml: “Many” is doing a tremendous amount of work there. Do you mean in absolute terms? It takes months to a year to evict a tenant for non-payment.
children.textZhHtml: “Many”正在那里做大量的工作。你是指绝对意义上的吗？因未付款而驱逐租户需要数月至一年的时间。
